description: Eliware Test deterministic convention-enforcement harness directive.

authoritativeFor: The standard harness for deterministic repository-convention enforcement.
The harness configuration, check identity, result, and validation contract.
notAuthoritativeFor: Semantic review, human approval, external registries, release authorization, deployment, or operations.

crosslinks.authoritativeFor: Repository authority and the E-18 namespace.
The convention directives this harness evaluates.

dos: Provide the standard Eliware repository-validation harness.
Enforce every convention requirement that can be validated deterministically or partially deterministically from repository, configuration, filesystem, process, or test evidence.
Leave requirements that cannot be validated even partially through deterministic evidence to the responsible human or semantic review process.
Use the authoritative convention specifications as the source of the requirements; do not duplicate those requirements in this specification.
donts: Do not define, reinterpret, or replace the conventions in the harness specification.
Do not infer which convention groups apply from repository contents or project shape.
Do not silently pass missing, malformed, unknown, duplicate, or unexpectedly skipped configuration or checks.
Do not expose internal checks, orchestrators, or utilities as the consumer runtime interface.

dos: Treat forks of non-Eliware repositories as exempt from Eliware conventions.
Do not require fork-specific check modules or apply Eliware convention checks to an excluded upstream fork.
donts: Do not create or execute src/checks/fork/* modules for repositories outside the Eliware convention boundary.

dos: Fail fast before convention-check discovery when package.json is missing or unreadable.
Fail fast before convention-check discovery when package.json.eliware is missing or malformed.
Fail fast when the declared convention baseline, applied groups, or exemption configuration is invalid or unsupported.
donts: Do not infer a default package, convention baseline, applied group, or exemption configuration.
Do not begin partial validation after a fatal package or convention-configuration error.

dos: Keep the public consumer interface at the eliware-test CLI.
Keep the CLI, orchestrators, checks, process adapters, diagnostics, and utilities as separate focused responsibilities.
donts: Do not require consumers to import internal implementation modules.

dos: Support the documented CLI modes and options through the public command.
Report failures with stable categories while preserving actionable diagnostics.
donts: Do not require consumers to know convention-specific module paths.

dos: Read the convention baseline, explicitly applied convention groups, and exact exemptions from package.json.eliware before selecting checks.
Apply only explicitly configured groups and exact rule exemptions.
donts: Do not infer applicability from dependencies, files, scripts, entrypoints, or runtime behavior.
Do not use broad or undocumented exemptions.

dos: Represent each deterministic or partially deterministic check as a separately identifiable module under src/checks/<group>/<id>.mjs.
Require the module filename, exported rule ID, and result rule ID to agree exactly.
donts: Do not create modules for requirements with no deterministic evidence path.
Do not let one module silently represent multiple unrelated requirements.

dos: Return only pass or fail for each check with a stable rule ID and actionable message.
Aggregate selected results without converting uncertainty into success.
Keep discovery, filesystem traversal, subprocess output, and user-facing paths bounded and normalized.
donts: Do not return warning, review, skipped, or unknown as a check outcome.
Do not silently ignore malformed or missing evidence.

dos: Preserve the established deterministic validation lifecycle and its focused-test, coverage, lint, package-check, and diagnostic behavior where it does not conflict with the authoritative conventions.
Run all applicable post-test validation stages needed to report actionable failures.
donts: Do not silently fall back from a requested focused validation to an unrelated broad validation.
Do not let an enforcement opt-out disable unrelated validation stages.

dos: Use native ESM and native Jest suites for the harness implementation and its tests.
Keep implementation tests beside the responsibility they directly exercise and keep orchestration tests focused on composition.
donts: Do not introduce alternate test frameworks or compatibility test harnesses.

dos: Preserve useful deterministic behavior from prior harness releases when it is compatible with the authoritative v8 conventions.
Keep unsupported semantic, approval-dependent, external-registry, and live-operational concerns outside deterministic check modules.
donts: Do not claim deterministic enforcement for a requirement without a reproducible evidence source.
Do not publish, tag, push, deploy, or perform other external state changes as an implicit validation side effect.
